Subject: Post-demo: request/response schema & streaming constraints for VelaHealth POC

Hi Anya —

Great to meet you and the VelaHealth team this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Goals: confirm POC acceptance criteria around latency (<300ms for single-turn lookup), reranking quality (top-5 precision), and cost targets.
2) Tech items we promised to follow up on: SDK bootstrap snippets for Node and Python, auth handshake options (API key vs short-lived token + mTLS), routing policy for failover between hosted and Dedicated, and the recommended request/response schema for chat-style interactions (structured output + tool-calling).
3) Immediate ask for you: share a sample conversation and a representative document to index for embeddings/rerank so we can size embeddings footprint.

I attached a short "MVP scope" PDF and a plain-text sample schema. Below is a pragmatic schema we think will minimize token usage while preserving structured outputs: 

--- sample-reqresp-schema (plain text) ---
{
  "type": "chat", /* or "completion" for single-turn */
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are VelaHealth assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Give me the eligibility summary for patient X"}
  ],
  "response_format": {
    "format": "json_schema",
    "schema": {"eligibility": "string", "confidence": "float", "references": ["string"]}
  },
  "max_tokens": 250, /* keep concise to control cost */
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "streaming": true /* enable streaming for first token to improve perceived latency */
}
--- end sample ---

Notes on tradeoffs: enabling streaming reduces time-to-first-byte but complicates client-side assembly when you need both structured JSON and tool calls. Our SDK offers a helper that reassembles streaming chunks and validates against the JSON schema on the client side. For reranking/embeddings, we recommend batching 64-128 docs for offline index builds and using 8-16 doc batches for on-demand rerank endpoints.

Proposed next steps: 
- You to share the sample conversation and a 1–2 GB slice of documents (or a URL where we can pull them).
- We send a short Node + Python SDK bootstrap (inc. auth examples) and a proposed routing policy YAML.
- Quick follow-up call next Tue 8/19 10am PT to finalize acceptance criteria.

Thanks — feel free to loop anyone else in.

Best,

Thanks Rafael — really helpful summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we hand off to our eng team: 

1) Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens issued by our identity provider (OIDC). Does Redwood support a token exchange flow (OIDC -> short Redwood token) and automatic rotation? Any docs you can share?
2) Streaming + structured JSON: our client displays partial results as they arrive and then runs validation against the final JSON. Will the SDK helper you mentioned emit a single validated JSON object or a stream of events (like "partial_payload", "schema_validated")?
3) Tokenization: for the eligibility summaries we expect lots of small fields. Can you advise on whether we should pack data into a single user message or multiple user messages to minimize token overhead?

We can provide a small sample dataset by EOD Friday. If you can do the SDK snippets + routing YAML before Monday that would help us schedule the POC.

Anya — quick answers inline below. I'm also copying Ben and Vanessa to coordinate the HubSpot deal and onboarding docs.

1) Auth: yes — we support an OIDC token exchange pattern. Typical flow: Vela issues an OIDC assertion -> Redwood STS exchanges for a short-lived Redwood session token (1h) -> client uses session token for requests. We also support mTLS for Dedicated deployments. I'll attach an example token-exchange diagram in the follow-up.

2) Streaming + structured JSON: our SDK emits an event stream of chunks during generation. The helper offers two modes: 
  - assemble_and_validate: returns a single validated JSON object (raises error if schema mismatch)
  - event_stream: emits incremental events (token, partial_text, tool_call, final_json_validated) so you can update UI progressively. Use assemble_and_validate when you must guarantee schema on final payload.

3) Tokenization and packing: packing small fields into a single user message reduces token overhead because it avoids repeated role metadata, but too-large single messages can push max_tokens up. For structured outputs, use concise keys and rely on json_schema output to keep responses compact. Example: prefer a single user message with delimitered fields when you expect short structured answers.

We'll send the Node/Python snippets plus routing policy and the token-exchange diagram by EOD Monday.

Rafael
